title: Introduction to HTML
subtitle: Learn how the web begins and build your first app screen
description: The complete beginner lesson. You will understand what HTML is, how websites work, and you will build your first real page that will grow into a full app by Lesson 10.

blocks.text: PAGE 1: Welcome - Let's Talk Like Humans
Hey! It's me, your Code Academy instructor. I know you're excited to build apps, and I'm going to be honest with you - every single app you use started exactly where you are right now.
YouTube? Started with HTML. Facebook? Started with HTML. Your Code Academy app you are using now? Built with HTML at its core. So you're in the right place.

Quick thing before we start - inside this app, you can actually write code. Go to your Home Page > Click the Menu tab (top corner) > Click on Practical or Practice. You will see a code editor there. Try all the codes I give you in this lesson THERE. Don't just read it, run it!
PAGE 2: What is HTML Really?

Okay so what is HTML? Forget the textbook definition for a second. Imagine you want to build a house. Before you paint it or add electricity, you need to build the walls, doors, windows, rooms. HTML does exactly that for websites.

HTML stands for HyperText Markup Language. HyperText means text that can link to other text - like when you click a link. Markup means you MARK the text to tell the browser: Hey, this is a heading, this is a paragraph, this is an image.
Important: HTML is NOT a programming language that thinks like Python or JavaScript. It doesn't do calculations. It's a structure language. It tells the browser WHAT to show, not HOW to think.

blocks.output:

This is marked as a link

blocks.question: In your own words, what does HTML do best?
options: It adds colors and animations alone
blocks.correctFeedback: Exactly! You got it. HTML = Structure. Like the skeleton of your app.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Not quite. Remember my house example? HTML builds the walls and structure. Colors are done by CSS later.
blocks.reasoning: HTML creates headings, paragraphs, images, buttons, links. It's the foundation everything else builds on.

blocks.text: PAGE 3: How Your Code Becomes a Website
Have you ever wondered what happens when you type google.com? Let me explain it in 10 seconds.

Step 1: Your browser (Chrome) goes to a computer called a Server and says 'Give me the HTML file for Google'. Step 2: The server sends the HTML file. Step 3: Your browser reads the HTML from top to bottom and draws the page you see. That's it!
That means YOU can create that file. When you write HTML and open it in Chrome, Chrome will render it as a real website. No internet needed for now.

blocks.text: If you save that text as .html and open it, the browser will show it. But it doesn't know what is heading or paragraph. That's why we need tags. Let's fix it.
PAGE 4: The 4 Parts of a Professional HTML Page
Every professional developer writes HTML with the same skeleton. It's like a standard form. If you learn this once, you can build 1000 websites. Let's look at it.

blocks.title: Example 3: Professional Skeleton - Copy this for all your projects
blocks.code:
Hello Code Academy!

This is my first real app screen.
blocks.output:
Hello Code Academy!
This is my first real app screen.

blocks.text: Let's break it down like gist: <!DOCTYPE html> tells Chrome 'Yo, this is modern HTML5, render it properly'. Without it, your page might break on some phones.

<html lang="en"> wraps EVERYTHING. <head> is the invisible part - it holds info ABOUT the page, like title, character set, and that very important viewport tag that makes your app look good on mobile. <body> is what the user SEES. Everything visible must be inside body.

This is wrong, won't show properly

This is correct, this WILL show on page
blocks.output: This is correct, this WILL show on page

blocks.question: Where MUST you put an <h1> so users can see it?
blocks.correctFeedback: Perfect! Body = Visible. Head = Invisible info. You are learning fast.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Remember: Head is for invisible information. Body is for visible content.
blocks.reasoning: All content users see must be in <body>. <head> contains metadata.

blocks.text: PAGE 6: Attributes - The Adjectives of HTML
If elements are nouns, attributes are adjectives. They give extra information. You always write them inside the opening tag. Let's make a link go somewhere - you need an attribute for that.

blocks.title: Example 7: href Attribute - Where should the link go?
blocks.code: Click to go to Google Visit My GitHub Go to About Page
blocks.output:
Click to go to Google
Visit My GitHub
Go to About Page

blocks.text: See? href tells the link where to go. Without href, <a> does nothing. Other important attributes are src for images (source), alt for image description, lang for language.

I have taught thousands of students in Ghana and outside. These 3 mistakes kill their progress - don't do them.

blocks.question: Which meta tag makes your app mobile-friendly?
blocks.correctFeedback: Brilliant! That viewport tag is what makes your final app look like a real app on phones.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: It's the viewport tag. Always include it in every project.
blocks.reasoning: viewport meta tag tells mobile browsers to use device width for proper responsive design.

blocks.text: PAGE 8: Practical Time - Build Your App's First Screen
Alright, enough theory. It's time to build. Remember what I told you at the start? Go now: Home Page > Menu Tab > Practical or Practice. Open the editor.
Your mission: Create the home screen of your final app. This same file will become your portfolio website by Lesson 10. Copy this, then change the name, bio, and links to YOURS.

PAGE 9: What You Have Achieved Today
Let's be real - today you did something big. Many people only watch videos. You actually built a page with doctype, html, head, body, h1, p, a, img, br. That's 8 different elements in one day!

Save that file as index.html somewhere safe. Every lesson from now on, we will open it and add more features - lists, tables, forms, everything - until it becomes a full website you can show to anyone.

blocks.question: Which part contains ALL the visible content of your app?
blocks.correctFeedback: Excellent! You now know the core structure. You're ready for Lesson 2.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Correct answer is <body>. Head is invisible.
blocks.reasoning: Body holds all visible content - headings, paragraphs, links, images.

blocks.text: PAGE 10: Lesson Complete - Prepare for Next Level
You have completed Introduction to HTML. You now understand what HTML is, how a browser works, the professional skeleton, elements, void elements, and attributes.
Your homework: Go to Menu > Practical and try to break and fix your code. What happens if you remove viewport? What happens if you forget ? Experiment - that's how real developers learn.

In Lesson 2: HTML Text and Headings, we will make your app look professional with proper headings, bold text, paragraphs, and lists. Your simple page will start looking like a real company website. See you there!
